text:
maria: Heads up — after the batching heuristic change on feature/kv-prefetch we saw a regression in tail latency in CI. nvprof traces were inconclusive (huge file, noisy). Can someone take an nsys capture focused on the prefetch+batch window?

kevin: I can run it. full-system traces blow up quickly though. suggestion: bracket with NVTX so we only capture the region where the sequence is created + kvcache populate. sampling helps too (we care about kernel-choice flips, not every memcpy). :mag_right:

jessie: Agree. My go-to for this is: short warmup, then bracket the real window with NVTX push/pop from the client, and use a sampling window to reduce qdrep size. Example python nvtx markers:```python
import nvtx
for i in range(5):
    nvtx.push("seq-start")
    run_one_request()
    nvtx.pop()
```
That makes --capture-range work nicely.

kevin: Example nsys CLI I used recently (adapted):```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/kv-prefetch.qdrep --sample-window=200us --duration=25s
# or bracketed: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o kv-bracket.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx --sample-window=200us --duration=40s
```
Note: --capture-range=nvtx tells nsys to align capture around NVTX push/pop so you don't need to guess offsets.

maria: Nice. Two specific things to look for: (1) kernel handoff where small attention kernels switch to kv-prefetch kernels mid-batch (we suspect scheduler is choosing the wrong kernel on the second micro-batch), (2) KV cache populate causing short-lived device-to-device memcpy storms.

jessie: When inspecting the timeline look for these patterns: repeated tiny kernel launches interleaved with memcpy H->D and D->D. If attention kernels degrade to a different kernel family (e.g., attention_fwd_small -> attention_fwd_generic) at some token length, that's our kernel-selection flip. Also check the NVTX names we annotate for batch boundaries — helps correlate kernel mix with request size.

kevin: I ran a quick capture (branch vs main) and uploaded to perf server: link: https://perf.redwood.local/q/4532109876. perf-bot: uploaded two traces (main vs feature/kv-prefetch) and generated a basic summary.

perf-bot: Summary: feature/kv-prefetch.qdrep size=1.2GB, main.qdrep size=700MB. Difference: +30% GPU idle spikes during batch boundary, +12% D2D memcpy tokens.

rick: For large captures consider using --stats-only first (`nsys stats`) to get high-level kernel counts, then sample+bracket only the interesting area. Also the qdrep diff tool (`nsys profile --report=summary`) can help with quick regressions.

maria: Good notes. One gotcha: if sample-window is too short you miss short-lived kernels, if too long you reintroduce noise. We found 100-500us works well for our micro-bursty inference. Jessie, can you try 2 bracketed captures with sample-window=150us and 400us and attach both?

jessie: On it. I'll also add an NVTX marker around the KV evict/populate call specifically so we can isolate the memcpy hotspot. Sample commands I'll run:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/kv-populate-150us.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx --sample-window=150us --duration=30s
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/kv-populate-400us.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx --sample-window=400us --duration=30s
```
and I'll keep the warmup loop to make the bracket stable.

kevin: Also try adding `--capture-offset` if your NVTX push/pop around warmup are noisy — shift window a bit so bracket lands on the steady-state batch. And enable OSRT trace so you get thread scheduling events (useful to see if host-side queueing causes micro-burst mismatches).

maria: Action items: kevin will diff main vs branch qdrep and post kernel-count table. jessie will run the two bracketed sampled captures with explicit NVTX around kv-populate. I'll grep kernels for name families and search for kernel-switch points.

kevin: Quick tip when comparing: export per-kernel stats to CSV with `nsys stats --report=kernel` and diff the rows. Look for changes in average duration and launch count for the tiny kernels — that indicates kernel-selection thrash.

perf-bot: Note: when posting qdrep links, include which PID/seed you used for the capture. Otherwise it's hard to map NVTX markers to the client runs.

maria: Thanks all. If we confirm it's a kernel-selection regression we'll try adding a lightweight warmup micro-batch that pins the chosen kernel (or adjust the kernel-selection heuristic) as a short-term mitigation.

jessie: Uploading first captures now, will follow with CSV exports.

kevin: I'll start a short run on a separate instance to reproduce locally and will post findings in this thread.

maria: perfect — ping here when the csv diffs are up. :thumbsup:
